name: Invoices & Credit Notes for WooCommerce
author: wpboxcz

sections.description:
Invoices & Credit Notes for WooCommerce issues an invoice for every paid order, saves it as a PDF and sends it to the customer. A refund gets a credit note. Everything is created and stored on your own site – no external invoicing service, no monthly fee, no account to create.

It works for shops anywhere. Shops in the European Union get the VAT details EU law asks for (reverse charge, OSS, VAT in the local currency); the plugin was born in the Czech Republic, so Czech and Slovak shops get everything their law wants out of the box.

Invoices without manual work

  • The invoice is issued automatically when the order is Processing (paid) or Completed – set per payment method. Cash on delivery waits for Completed, after the customer has taken the parcel. You can also issue it by hand in the order.
  • Optional order status Shipped for orders on the way (cash on delivery: Processing → Shipped → Completed).
  • A cancelled or failed order that already has an invoice gets a credit note for the whole invoice.
  • Your own number series with year, month and padding, e.g. INV2026-0001. The sequence can restart every year. Numbers are assigned atomically – no gaps and no duplicates, even with many orders at the same time.
  • The PDF is attached to the WooCommerce emails you choose and the customer finds it in My Account → Orders.
  • The orders list shows the invoice number; the order screen has an Invoice box with Issue invoice, Open PDF and Redraw PDF.

Credit notes

A refund in WooCommerce issues a credit note for the order’s invoice automatically: its own number series, negative amounts, a reference to the corrected invoice. The PDF goes with the refund email and to My Account.

Taxes done right

  • Rates and amounts come straight from WooCommerce – VAT, sales tax or GST, including the OSS rates of the customer’s EU country.
  • Tax recapitulation by rates on every invoice.
  • Suppliers in Europe see “VAT”, elsewhere the documents say “Tax”.
  • Not registered for VAT or sales tax? The plugin issues a plain invoice without tax.

For EU shops

  • An EU business with a VAT ID and no VAT charged gets a reverse-charge invoice with the sentence of Art. 196 of the VAT Directive.
  • Customers outside the EU get the sentence about a supply outside the EU.
  • An invoice in a foreign currency shows the VAT base and VAT in your local currency, as Art. 91 of the VAT Directive wants: at the European Central Bank rate (euro countries in EUR, Poland in PLN, Hungary in HUF …), Czech shops in CZK at the Czech National Bank rate. The rate is stored with the invoice. Downloading the rates is off until you turn it on in the settings.
  • Each currency can have its own bank account on the invoice.

Safe for accounting

  • An issued invoice never changes – the plugin keeps a frozen copy of all its data. A correction is a credit note.
  • PDFs are stored in a protected folder with a random name. Customers download them only through a link checked against their account or the order key.
  • Uninstalling the plugin never deletes invoices, their data or the numbering – you must keep invoices for years.

Languages and look

  • The document language follows the order: the language of the checkout, else the site language for domestic customers and English for the others (or a fixed language).
  • Number and date formats follow the document language.
  • Included translations: English, Czech, Slovak. Other languages can be added on translate.wordpress.org.
  • Your logo, accent colour, note and footer. Check the result with Preview a sample invoice (PDF).
  • Company ID and VAT ID of the customer are read from the fields of common checkout plugins.

Compatibility

  • High-Performance Order Storage (HPOS) and the block checkout.
  • MySQL, MariaDB and SQLite (WordPress Playground).
  • The PDF is made on your server with the bundled Dompdf library.

Pro add-on

Need to send the invoices to your accountant? The paid add-on WPBox – Invoices Pro adds the export to accounting: LPsoft PROFIT, ISDOC (the Czech e-invoice standard) and CSV for the book of issued invoices and the OSS return. This plugin works fully without it.

External services

The plugin can download official exchange rates, only to show the VAT base and VAT in the supplier’s local currency on invoices in a foreign currency (EU VAT law requires it). This is off by default – nothing is downloaded until the shop owner ticks “Download official exchange rates for invoices in a foreign currency” in Invoices → Supplier. Even then, shops that invoice only in their local currency, shops outside the EU and suppliers not registered for VAT never contact these services. The rate is cached per day. No order, customer or site data is sent – only a request for the rate list.

European Central Bank – suppliers in EU countries other than the Czech Republic:

  • What is sent: a request for the reference rates of the last 90 days (or the full history for older dates).
  • Service: https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/eurofxref/eurofxref-hist-90d.xml
  • Terms of use: https://www.ecb.europa.eu/services/disclaimer/html/index.en.html
  • Privacy policy: https://www.ecb.europa.eu/home/data-protection/privacy-statements/website/html/index.en.html

Czech National Bank – suppliers in the Czech Republic:

  • What is sent: a request for the daily rate list with the date of the taxable supply in the URL (denni_kurz.txt?date=DD.MM.YYYY).
  • Service: https://www.cnb.cz/cs/financni-trhy/devizovy-trh/kurzy-devizoveho-trhu/kurzy-devizoveho-trhu/denni_kurz.txt
  • Terms of use: https://www.cnb.cz/en/privacy-statement-and-disclaimer/disclaimer-copyright/
  • Privacy policy: https://www.cnb.cz/en/privacy-statement-and-disclaimer/

Third-party libraries

  • Dompdf 3.1.6 – LGPL-2.1 – https://github.com/dompdf/dompdf
  • php-font-lib 1.0.2 – LGPL-2.1 – https://github.com/dompdf/php-font-lib
  • php-svg-lib 1.0.2 – LGPL-3.0 – https://github.com/dompdf/php-svg-lib
  • masterminds/html5 2.12.0 – MIT – https://github.com/Masterminds/html5-php
  • sabberworm/php-css-parser 8.9.0 – MIT – https://github.com/MyIntervals/PHP-CSS-Parser
  • DejaVu fonts – Bitstream Vera / DejaVu licence

The libraries are bundled under the prefix WPBI\Vendor so they never clash with another plugin’s copy.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin (WooCommerce must be active).
  2. Open WooCommerce → Invoices and fill in the supplier details.
  3. Choose the numbering pattern and when the invoice is issued.
  4. Check the look with “Preview a sample invoice (PDF)”.
sections.faq:
Can I use it outside the EU?

Yes. The plugin takes the taxes WooCommerce calculated (sales tax, GST …) and the documents say “Tax”. The EU sentences and the currency conversion are only used by suppliers in the EU.

I am not registered for VAT. Can I use it?

Yes. Untick Registered for VAT or another sales tax in the Supplier tab and the invoices are issued without tax.

How does OSS work?

The plugin takes the VAT rate WooCommerce charged in the order. Set the OSS rates of the EU countries in WooCommerce → Settings → Tax and the invoices follow them.

When does an invoice get reverse charge?

When the supplier is in the EU, the customer is a business from another EU country with a VAT ID and WooCommerce charged no VAT (for example with a plugin that checks the VAT ID in VIES and makes the customer VAT exempt).

Which exchange rate is used?

For a supplier in the Czech Republic the Czech National Bank rate for the date of the taxable supply. For other EU countries the last European Central Bank rate published before that date. The rate and its date are printed on the invoice. Turn on “Exchange rates” in Invoices → Supplier first; without it invoices show amounts only in the order currency.

Can I change an invoice after it was issued?

No, and that is on purpose: invoices must not change. Issue a credit note (a refund in the order) and a new invoice if needed. Redraw PDF only applies a new look, the content stays.

Where are the PDF files stored?

In a folder with a random name in wp-content/uploads, protected against direct access. Customers download them through a link checked against their account or the secret order key.

What happens to invoices when I uninstall the plugin?

Nothing. Invoices must be kept for years, so the plugin never deletes them, their data or the numbering.

I used WPBox – Invoices before. How do I switch?

This is the same plugin under its WordPress.org name. Install it, deactivate WPBox – Invoices and activate this one – settings, invoices and the numbering stay. Then delete the old plugin folder by FTP (or with the Delete button – the uninstall keeps all invoices).
sections.changelog:
2.3.0

  • Downloading exchange rates (European Central Bank, Czech National Bank) is now opt-in: new setting “Exchange rates” in the Supplier tab, off by default. Turn it on if you invoice in a foreign currency and need VAT in your local currency.
  • Admin styles and scripts moved to enqueued files.
  • Dompdf 3.1.6.

2.2.0

  • When to issue the invoice can be set per payment method (Processing or Completed). Cash on delivery defaults to Completed: the invoice is issued only after the customer has taken the parcel. A Completed order always gets the invoice.
  • New order status Shipped (can be turned off) with a bulk action in the order list: cash on delivery goes Processing → Shipped → Completed; a returned parcel goes to Cancelled and gets no invoice.
  • Cash on delivery is printed as paid only once the order is Completed, with that date as the date of supply (WooCommerce counts it as paid already in Processing).
  • An order that already has an invoice and is Cancelled or Failed gets a credit note for the whole invoice automatically (can be turned off). When partial credit notes exist, the order gets a note instead.
  • The plugin description in the list of plugins is translated (Czech, Slovak).
  • New filters: wpbi_trigger_status, wpbi_invoice_paid, wpbi_cancel_credit_data.

2.1.0

  • Look tab: the looks are shown as pictures; Preview opens a sample invoice in that look with your logo and accent colour right on the page – nothing is saved until you click Save Changes. “Preview a sample invoice (PDF)” also uses the unsaved choices.
  • Looks can bring a preview image (key “thumb” in the filter wpbi_templates).
  • Shorter label for the date of the taxable supply, so it fits on one line in every look (English “Supply date”, Czech “Datum zdan. plnění”, Slovak “Dátum dodania”).

2.0.1

  • Plugin header: no Plugin URI (it was the same as the Author URI).

2.0.0

  • New name for WordPress.org: Invoices & Credit Notes for WooCommerce (folder and text domain invoices-credit-notes-for-woocommerce; was WPBox – Invoices). Settings, invoices and numbering stay – deactivate the old plugin and activate this one.
  • For shops anywhere: suppliers outside Europe get “Tax” instead of “VAT” on the documents; the EU sentences (reverse charge, supply outside the EU) only for EU suppliers; “Tax document” only for Czech and Slovak suppliers.
  • VAT in the local currency for every EU country: Czech Republic in CZK at the Czech National Bank rate (as before), other EU countries at the European Central Bank rate (euro countries in EUR, Poland in PLN …). Slovak shops invoicing in EUR no longer get a CZK conversion.
  • Number and date format of the document language (set by the translation), e.g. “Nov 17, 2026” and “$1,234.50” in English.
  • Language of the document for domestic customers: the language of the site.
  • Payment reference instead of the Czech variable symbol for suppliers outside CZ and SK.

1.4.2

  • Numbering works on SQLite too (WordPress Playground, SQLite Database Integration) – before, every number there was 0000.
  • Admin: the bank accounts table and the accent colour field are laid out better.
  • Invoice: each contact of the supplier stays on one line.
  • Longer description, FAQ, screenshots, banner and icon for the plugin page on WordPress.org; vendor libraries documented in composer.json.

1.4.1

  • Preparation for WordPress.org: “Tested up to” only in readme.txt (tested with WordPress 7.1), coding standards of the Plugin Check tool.

1.4.0

  • The export to accounting (LPsoft PROFIT, ISDOC, CSV) moved to the paid add-on WPBox – Invoices Pro. The Export tab is gone from this plugin; the PROFIT settings and the “exported” marks of documents are kept and the add-on uses them.

1.3.1

  • PROFIT: new option “Registered for OSS” (off by default). Without it, sales to consumers in other EU countries are exported as domestic (Czech VAT below the EU limit of 10 000 EUR); with it in the OSS regime §110/2.

1.3.0

  • Export for LPsoft PROFIT: XML in PROFIT’s own format (Windows-1250) and a ready import template (.defx) with the invoice type (number series) and bank accounts per currency; PROFIT numbers the documents, the web number becomes the external number.
  • Invoicing regime, customer country, exchange rate, payment and paid amount for PROFIT.

1.2.0

  • Credit notes: a refund issues a credit note for the invoice (own numbering series, reference to the invoice, PDF in the refund email and My Account).
  • Export for accounting: ISDOC 6.0.2 (one XML or a ZIP of .isdoc files, foreign currency with the CNB rate) and CSV with VAT in CZK; documents can be marked as exported.

1.1.0

  • Bank account per currency (CZK, EUR, USD…). An empty row takes the WooCommerce Direct bank transfer account with the currency code in its name, else the default account.

1.0.0

  • First version: invoices for paid orders, numbering series, VAT (OSS, reverse charge, outside the EU, non-VAT-payer), CZK conversion at the Czech National Bank rate, PDF in emails and My Account, look “Classic” with logo and accent colour, English, Czech and Slovak.
